title: Which goth aesthetic are you?
blurb: Trad Goth, Romantic Goth, Nu-Goth, Cybergoth and more. Statements about darkness, style and where you belong.

questions.text: Old factories and concrete have a grim kind of beauty.
Lace, velvet and heavy fabrics are what I'd love to wear.
A sharp, all-black outfit with one silver detail beats lace and frills.
Neon, black PVC and a high-tech look are more me than anything old-fashioned.
Cute things with a creepy twist are my favourite.
Memories of hanging out at the mall in band shirts make me smile.
Going out to goth nights with my scene matters a lot to me.
Old small towns far from the city feel haunted in a way I like.
Gothic poems about death and lost love move me more than happy songs.
A cosy, cluttered room with candles and crystals sounds perfect.
Victorian mourning dress and old cathedrals pull me in more than anything modern.
Gardens, forests and graveyards feel calmer to me than cities.
An elegant, Victorian-style dark look matters more to me than a tough, ripped one.
Ripped fishnets and scuffed boots look better to me than a polished outfit.
My dark look is always neat, sharp and carefully put together.
Old records and the original eighties scene are my thing.
I'd rather keep to myself than be part of a scene.
Old church rituals and family traditions, even the strange ones, matter to me.
Looking different from everyone around me is a big part of being goth for me.
Ghost stories, the occult and the unexplained are a big part of what I love.
Bright colours have a place in a dark wardrobe.
I'm more into where goth is going next than into how it used to be.
I'd rather be alone in nature than out at a club.
New trends and the latest goth looks online are a big part of my style.
Ruins overgrown with ivy are more beautiful to me than any new building.
Vampires, ghosts and dark fairy tales feel more real to me than everyday life.
